image_description: A close-up, low-angle shot of a hammerhead shark swimming in dark blue water. The shark is viewed from below and the side, highlighting its white ventral surface and the underside of its cephalofoil. The distinctive T-shaped head is prominent, with one eye clearly visible at the tip. Other sharks are visible in the blurred background.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the laterally expanded, dorsoventrally flattened cephalofoil (hammer-shaped head).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the iconic laterally expanded, flat head structure characteristic of hammerhead sharks.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned at the extreme lateral tips of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible eye is located precisely at the outer extremity of the hammer structure, matching biological anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned near the lateral margins of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The angle of the shot (from below) and the resolution do not allow for clear visualization of the nostrils on the ventral side of the cephalofoil.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Anterior margin of the cephalofoil is straight to slightly curved with a central indentation in some species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The leading edge of the hammer appears straight and smooth, consistent with the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is streamlined and laterally compressed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the torso shows a smooth, tapered shape typical of pelagic sharks.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dorsal coloration is grey to brownish with white ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The underside is bright white, transitioning to a darker grey on the sides, exhibiting correct countershading.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is covered in dermal denticles with a rough texture.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image resolution and lighting are insufficient to resolve microscopic dermal denticles; the skin appears smooth.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: First dorsal fin is tall and falcate (sickle-shaped), positioned anteriorly.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal fin is on the top side of the shark and is completely occluded by the body in this ventral view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Pectoral fins are broad and triangular.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The pectoral fin on the right side is visible, appearing broad and triangular as expected.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caudal fin is asymmetrical with a pronounced upper lobe.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is either out of frame or too blurred in the background to assess structural asymmetry accurately.

artifact_observations.location: Ventral surface of the cephalofoil and throat area
artifact_observations.reasoning: The skin texture appears excessively smooth and plastic-like, lacking the subtle micro-texture or pore details expected in high-fidelity macro photography of shark skin. There is a slight 'waxy' sheen inconsistent with wet biological tissue.

The background sharks exhibit a uniform, smudged blur that lacks optical depth-of-field characteristics (bokeh). They appear more like painted shapes than out-of-focus objects, suggesting potential generation artifacts in background rendering.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species classification and rule out hybrid or malformed morphologies.
To verify the continuity of the cephalofoil and ensure no fusion artifacts exist between the head and the water/background.
To analyze the suspected plastic-like skin texture and background blur for signs of AI generation vs. photographic noise.

focus_areas: Cephalofoil structural integrity and eye placement
Skin texture realism (dermal denticles vs. smooth plastic)
Boundary sharpness between shark and water
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the skin texture on the white underbelly. Real shark skin has a specific grain even when smooth; AI often renders this as pure, noiseless white or plastic. Check if the eye reflects the environment correctly or if it looks like a flat sticker. Verify the background sharks don't have melted fins.
